title: Integration and End-to-End Project Verification
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and value of Integration and End-to-End Project Verification.
Apply integration and end-to-end project verification to a Python project scenario.
Identify decisions and trade-offs relevant to integration and end-to-end project verification.
Review common mistakes and risks in integration and end-to-end project verification.
Produce a verifiable project artifact using integration and end-to-end project verification principles.

understand.concept: Integration tests verify connected components such as services, repositories and adapters. End-to-end tests exercise important user journeys through the application's public interface. Test environments should be controlled, repeatable and separated from production data.
understand.whyItMatters: Testing component interactions catches defects that isolated unit tests cannot reveal.
understand.analogy: A relay team must verify both each runner and the handoff between runners.
understand.analogyLimit: End-to-end tests are slower and more brittle than unit tests, so they should focus on high-value workflows.
understand.summary: Integration and End-to-End Project Verification helps learners deliver and maintain reliable Python projects.

explain.narrative: Choose a small number of critical user journeys. Prepare isolated test data, deterministic external-service substitutes and cleanup rules. Verify persistence, error propagation and user-visible results. Keep unit tests for detailed edge cases and use integration or end-to-end tests where boundaries matter.
